# map.yaml: Typed Standards' technical relations to public projects, in three rings.
# After this comment, one header document, then one YAML document per edge. Outside x-typedstandards,
# each edge uses only the field names the SciOS core-and-satellite examples show for an edge
# (id, createdAt, subject, object). Every other field is under x-typedstandards.
# Written by corpus/pin.mjs from corpus/sources.json and corpus/manifest.json. This file's exact bytes
# are the output of one signed Typed Standards record in package/.
---
x-typedstandards:
  map: "Typed Standards: relations to public projects"
  domain: analysis-provenance
  subject: typedstandards.org
  createdAt: "2026-09-22"
  writtenFrom:
    sources: corpus/sources.json
    manifest: corpus/manifest.json
    manifestSha256: 2c23dafb122ed6dd7f1acb5f82296ccce65079417a29a898589aa9fcbba77980
  edgeTypes: The published schema shows one edge type, orbits, from a satellite to a core. This map has no orbits edge. No core record exists in this domain to be the object of one, and the model says a core is never a satellite. Each edge names its relation in x-typedstandards.relation, because the published schema has no edge type for any of these relations.
  relations:
    builds-on: The subject implements, or normatively uses, the object's published specification or code.
    complements: The two address different layers or artifact classes of one job and can be used together. Neither depends on the other.
    could-emit: The subject's own public text states an intent to produce Typed Standards records, cited by URL and date.
    adjacent: A related problem space. Neither depends on the other, and there is no public statement of an intent to emit or evaluate Typed Standards records.
  rings:
    1: Standards the specification builds on.
    2: Adjacent standards, drafts and proposals.
    3: Implementations, possible emitters, and agent runtimes.
  refs: Each ref is either a file at a 40-character commit SHA, a dated W3C TR URL, an rfc-editor.org text URL, or a published npm release tarball. A ref gives both the location and the SHA-256 of the bytes that location served when it was fetched. Where a project has no immutable location, the ref gives the location, a null sha256, and the reason in x-typedstandards.pin.
  dropped:
    - name: DSSE (Dead Simple Signing Envelope)
      seed: Ring 1, listed with in-toto
      reason: "Typed Standards uses neither the DSSE envelope nor its pre-authentication encoding. It signs an Ed25519ph signature over the envelope-hash hex string (specification §8.3.1). The specification does name DSSE: its adjacent-standards table lists in-toto / DSSE (§5.5), and Appendix C lists DSSE as a candidate envelope-serialization profile for in-toto-native consumers. Nothing is built on it. The in-toto entry covers the conventions the specification does use."
